background.executionContext:
**Commands used:**
1. `./b4w.ps1 help` — learned available commands
2. `./b4w.ps1 goto "https://www.amazon.com/"` — navigated to Amazon (daemon auto-started)
3. `./b4w.ps1 snapshot -v 0 --stdout` — captured accessibility tree to find search box (`e143331`)
4. `./b4w.ps1 fill e143331 "pens to draw on whiteboards" --submit` — searched (single command!)
5. `./b4w.ps1 snapshot -v 0 --stdout` — attempted to read results (63KB output, too large)
6. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot capture` — captured HTML snapshot with interactive elements list
7. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot inspect` — attempted auto-discovery (picked up navigation, not products)
8. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all text "a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-4" --limit 10` — extracted titles
9. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all text "span.a-price-whole" --limit 10` — extracted prices
10. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all text "span.a-icon-alt" --limit 10` — extracted ratings
11. `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all attr "a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-4" href --limit 10` — extracted URLs
12. Manually correlated the four arrays and composed the comparison markdown

**Key decisions:**
- Used interactive elements list from `htmlsnapshot capture` to identify product title CSS selectors (`a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-4`) instead of `htmlsnapshot inspect` which picked up navigation patterns
- Used `--submit` flag on `fill` to combine typing + Enter into one command
- Manually matched title/price/rating/URL arrays since `get all` calls are independent
- Skipped review count extraction after two selector attempts failed

**Workarounds required:**
- Avoided reading full snapshot (63KB) — used `htmlsnapshot` commands instead
- Used the interactive elements summary from `htmlsnapshot capture` to discover selectors when `inspect` failed
- Manually correlated four independent extraction results

issues.title: No built-in product card extraction for e-commerce pages

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Try to extract correlated product data (title + price + rating + URL) from an Amazon/Best Buy/Walmart search results page.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A single command or documented workflow that produces a table of product data: `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot extract-products` or `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query --preset amazon-search`.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: User must: manually discover selectors for each field (often requiring Amazon-specific CSS knowledge), run 4+ separate `get all` commands, and manually correlate the arrays — which is error-prone and time-consuming. The SKILL.md explicitly warns: 'Multiple get all calls produce unaligned arrays.'

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The extraction system is powerful but low-level. There is no abstraction for the common 'extract product listings from a search results page' use case. X-SQL can do correlated extraction but requires writing a full SQL query with domain-specific functions (DOM_FIRST_TEXT, DOM_FIRST_ATTR), which is a steep learning curve for a first-time user.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add an `htmlsnapshot extract-products` command with built-in heuristics for common e-commerce patterns (product cards with title/price/rating/image)
- Provide preset X-SQL templates for Amazon, eBay, Walmart, etc. in the documentation
- Add a `--correlate` flag to `get all` that groups results by parent container when given multiple selectors
- Document the X-SQL approach more prominently in the core loop section of SKILL.md

sections.label: Reproduction

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect defaults to analyzing wrong DOM pattern

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot inspect (with no selector argument) on an Amazon search results page

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Auto-discovery identifies the most prominent repeating pattern — product cards with title, price, rating — and suggests selectors for them.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Analyzed <div> elements and picked up navigation keyboard shortcut elements from a hidden shortcuts menu as the repeating pattern. Suggested selectors like `span.shortcut-key.nav-assistant-card-font` which are useless for product extraction.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The inspect command defaults to analyzing `div` elements. The hidden navigation menu (`#shortcut-menu`) contains repeating div structures that score high as a pattern. Product cards on Amazon use complex nested divs and the inspect heuristics don't prioritize visible, high-value content areas over hidden navigation.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/ — htmlsnapshot inspect logic (likely in an HTML snapshot analysis service)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Prioritize visible content areas over hidden/offscreen elements (the navigation was at box=-9988, clearly offscreen)
- Weight elements by viewport visibility and text content richness
- When inspect is called without arguments, try multiple common container selectors (div[data-*], li, article) and report the best
- Allow `htmlsnapshot inspect "div[data-component-type]"` to be documented as the recommended pattern for Amazon-style product grids

issues.title: htmlsnapshot capture then get workflow requires Amazon-specific CSS knowledge

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: New user tries to extract product data from Amazon without knowing Amazon's CSS class naming conventions.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Documentation or tool output guides the user to the right selectors for common sites, or the tool auto-discovers them.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: User must know that Amazon product titles use `a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-4`, prices use `span.a-price-whole`, ratings use `span.a-icon-alt`. The `htmlsnapshot capture` interactive elements summary helped discover these, but the connection between 'interactive elements' and data extraction is not obvious to a first-time user.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The interactive elements list from `htmlsnapshot capture` shows CSS selectors as a side effect of listing clickable elements. This is an accidental discovery path — it's not documented as a way to find extraction selectors.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Document the pattern explicitly in SKILL.md: 'After htmlsnapshot capture, look at the Interactive Elements list for CSS class names you can use with htmlsnapshot get'
- Add a 'Common selectors found' section to htmlsnapshot capture output that groups elements by their CSS classes and suggests which to use for data extraction
- Add site-specific recipe docs (or link to htmlsnapshot-scenarios.md more prominently)
